prompt: Let $R\subseteq A\times A$, with all quantified variables ranging over $A$. Which property is defined exactly by $\forall x\exists y\; R(x,y)$?

answers.explanation: Each element has at least one outgoing related element, which may be itself.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
One related pair suffices; the other elements may be isolated. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
An element has at most one outgoing related element; it need not have any. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every pair of distinct elements is comparable in at least one direction. This convention imposes no condition on loops. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.

answers.text: Existence of an incoming neighbour for every element.
answers.explanation: Every element has a predecessor; this does not ensure that every element has a successor. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.

answers.text: Existence of one common outgoing target.
answers.explanation: One element must be a successor of every element; seriality can use different successors. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every ordered pair is present, including every loop. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
